title: Daily Health Briefing
intro: Good morning! Here's today's research digest across your tracked topics — anti-aging, HIIT for women, pelvic floor training, integrative options for HER2+ breast cancer, and sleep. Each section leads with the practical takeaway and the strength of the evidence, with linked citations below. Informational only — talk to a clinician before acting on anything here.

sections.body:
This week leans toward **topical mitophagy** and a useful reality check on supplements.

- **Topical urolithin A.** A new *iScience* paper (published Oct 16, 2026) reports that in **randomized, placebo-controlled** human studies a topical urolithin A (Mitopure) formulation **reduced periorbital wrinkle depth after 8 weeks** and **calmed UVB-induced redness**, alongside lab evidence of activated mitophagy and lower senescence markers. Promising, but note the studies were **industry-sponsored** (Amazentis/L'Oréal).
- **Supplement reality check.** A *Frontiers in Pharmacology* review frames popular "longevity" compounds — **resveratrol, curcumin, urolithin A** — as real mitochondrial regulators that are hobbled by **poor oral absorption**. Practically: expect **modest** effects from pills, and favor well-formulated or delivery-optimized products over mega-doses.

sources.title: Topical application of urolithin A activates mitophagy and enhances mitochondrial function to promote skin longevity

sections.body:
The newest evidence keeps HIIT as a **time-efficient** tool for fitness and body composition — with a clear "don't lose muscle" caveat.

- **Body composition & fitness.** A 2026 systematic review & meta-analysis (15 RCTs) in *Frontiers in Physiology* found HIIT significantly lowered **body weight, BMI, body-fat %, and fat mass** and sharply improved **VO₂max** in women with overweight/obesity. Effects on cholesterol were mixed, and the authors rate overall certainty as low — so treat it as a reliable *fitness and recomposition* tool, not a guaranteed lipid fix.
- **Pairing with fasting.** A 131-woman 2×2 **RCT** (*British Journal of Nutrition*) testing time-restricted eating ± HIIT found **no added synergy**, and the fasting arm trimmed fat **but also lost some muscle**. Takeaway: keep **protein and resistance work** in the mix so intensity builds, rather than costs, lean mass.

sources.title: Effects of HIIT on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and selected lipid outcomes in adult women with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis

sections.body:
**Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)** stays the evidence-based first-line choice — and two fresh RCTs sharpen *how* to do it well.

- **PFMT beats Pilates.** An Oct 15, 2026 **RCT** (*International Urogynecology Journal*) in women with stress incontinence found targeted PFMT dropped the incontinence-impact score by **−4.4 points vs just −0.7 for Pilates**, with much larger gains in pelvic-floor strength. Core/Pilates work is a nice add-on, but **direct pelvic-floor training is what moves the needle**.
- **Menopause matters.** A 2026 *Menopause* **RCT** showed that **supervised PFMT plus targeted education** eased genitourinary symptoms, incontinence impact, and strength more than education alone. The theme across both: **correct technique + coaching + consistency** beat unguided reps.

sources.title: Pelvic Floor Muscle Training Outperforms Pilates in Women with Stress Urinary Incontinence: A Randomized Controlled Trial

sections.topic: Integrative Options — HER2+ / TP53 Breast Cancer
sections.body:
Read "alternative" here as **evidence-based options to pair with standard care** — never as a replacement for it.

- **The standard-of-care story is the good news.** A new *Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology* review (Oct 8, 2026) notes HER2-positive disease is now **highly curable early-stage**, with the antibody-drug conjugate **trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)** moving into earlier lines; the field is even **de-escalating** treatment for low-risk tumors. A 2026 *NEJM* review echoes this rapid progress. Because germline **TP53 (p53)** changes are tied to early-onset breast cancer, genetics-informed care matters.
- **Supplements — stay grounded.** A 2026 cross-sectional study (*Int. J. Molecular Sciences*) found **no link between vitamin D status and tumor proliferation (Ki-67)**, a reminder to temper enthusiasm for single supplements and **coordinate anything integrative with your oncology team** to avoid interactions.

sources.title: Right-sizing treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer: evolving algorithms across the disease continuum

sections.body:
For restless or broken sleep, 2026 guidance still puts **behavioral therapy ahead of pills**.

- **CBT-I, now on your phone.** A 2026 **RCT** (*Internet Interventions*, 165 adults) of a fully automated **smartphone CBT-I** program produced a **clinically meaningful drop in insomnia severity** (effect size ~0.66), plus better sleep quality and fewer night-time awakenings — and more app engagement meant bigger gains.
- **About the medications.** New German/Austrian sleep-society recommendations note **~1 in 4** chronic hypnotic users become dependent; **melatonin, orexin antagonists (e.g., daridorexant), and antihistamines** can usually be stopped without tapering, while **Z-drugs/benzodiazepines need a slow 10–25%/week taper**, with CBT-I as support. A 2026 reanalysis also **downgraded** an earlier daridorexant suicidal-ideation signal (likely confounded by depression).
- **Supplements, honestly.** **Melatonin** is best for **circadian issues** (jet lag, shift work) and mild sleep-onset trouble, with low dependence; evidence for magnesium remains limited.

Best-practice habits: keep a **fixed wake time**, reserve the bed for sleep, dim screens before bed, and see a provider if disruption lasts beyond a few weeks (to rule out sleep apnea).
